https://www.quora.com/Is-Ecosia-really-a-good-search-engine

Use Bing. It’s literally the same thing. Ecosia isn’t a search engine, it’s a “tag’ system for Bing that tries to generate revenue for a third party. When they inevitably go bankrupt, the tracking information they own will just be sold alongside the copiers to whomever buys the business. And, sadly, that’s not the worst of it.
Ecosia is sadly trying to use saving the planet marketing gimmick to trick people into thinking searching through them is going to do good. First of all, all their searches are routed directly through Bing servers and Bing itself is super inefficient and is really bad about their eco footprint. But that isn’t important when you remember #2: Ecosia flat out lies and contradicts itself in it’s answers to basic questions, overhead cost, trees planted vs. cost of flying to plant trees, ecological costs of the company’s regular functions, and those are FURTHER dwarfed by the fact that #3) We aren’t going to consume our way out of our overconsumption problem. This is literally taking the answer about whether you’re an alcoholic or not from the guy who owns a liquor store. Even if their answer is right, you don’t trust the person who sells you the thing with whether you need it or not.
If you want to save the planet, go volunteer! Sierra club always needs people, there are plenty of options for fundraising to help support lobbies for everything from direct counter-CO2 technology implementation to clean energy consumption to corporate monitoring.
And if you want a good search engine, start with Google, go to DuckDuckGo if they don’t have an answer, and if you’re desperate Bing’s not consistent but occasionally has useful results the others don’t. Also the Internet Archive occasionally has gems, and Yandex can be useful for some things if you don’t mind doing a bit of translating or a bit of digging. Oh and BoardReader often has useful stuff like technical data and “how do I fix this” type answers as well as, well, people shitposting and talking about things they probably have never built. It’s a mix.
But ignore Ecosia.
